epic.intent:
Make Dark Mechanicus reject unsupported completion claims and deliver exactly the source that was verified, then reduce the coordination work agents must perform. The owner should be able to trust accepted tickets and sprint increments, recover interrupted runs through explicit actions, and choose a persistent single worker or parallel workers according to task coupling.

Order: (1) acceptance, artifact and increment invariants; (2) runtime-produced check receipts and evidence freshness; (3) scoped worker authority, lifecycle supervision, integration state and direct recovery; (4) task-appropriate execution, failure-aware routing, explicit capability constraints and a reproducible comparison.

Preserve human checkpoint authority, immutable historical evidence, provider neutrality, portable repository records, separate integration worktrees and existing external-host support. Each work ticket uses TDD and targeted checks; each sprint has one Fireguard ticket followed by its acceptance node running the full project Definition of Done once. Native/process/IPC changes also require a real packaged/Electron-path exercise before acceptance.

Do not modify or adopt revisions of the in-flight Source control epic. Execute on a dedicated feature branch from the integrated base selected at run start. Planning creates no branch or run. Completed Scrum cadence work is provenance, not state to copy.

The existing SPACE scorecards epic (ep_01m452vt115eqccd1ypdd596fy) owns comprehensive usage/timing ingestion, grades and scorecard UI. Reuse its observation contract when present; otherwise this epic's evaluation records raw measurements with explicit unavailable fields and no claimed cost savings. Learned model routing, mandatory independent-model review, OS-level sandboxing and cross-repository automation are outside this epic.

successCriteria.text: New acceptance decisions require complete explicit reviewer results for the pinned criteria and verified expected artifacts; missing, duplicate, unknown or unmet criterion evidence cannot unlock dependent tickets, while completed historical records retain their original hashes.

Sprint delivery is verified against a durable integration manifest and tested source identity; unrelated or incomplete commits, stale evidence and post-check source changes fail closed, and the existing unrelated-commit reproduction cannot pass.

Required check results have runtime-produced, immutable receipts tied to source identity, command and outcome; forged, failed, skipped or stale receipts cannot satisfy gates, and Fireguard evidence is reused only for the verified source.

Hosted workers cannot exercise orchestrator or reviewer authority, and a deterministic supervisor renews only live worker leases, records worker/worktree lifecycle and survives interruption without duplicate work or automatic acceptance.

A concise next-actions view and explicit recovery commands resolve checkpoint leftovers and stale integration evidence without undocumented pause/resume sequences or relaxing human approval and retry limits.

Cohesive work can reuse one worker context while independent work can run in parallel; both retain ticket attempts, review and checkpoint invariants, failures are classified before escalation, and unsupported hard constraints are explicit rather than silently satisfied.

A reproducible comparison of single-worker, current orchestration and adaptive execution reports actual quality outcomes, coordination calls, elapsed time and available usage with explicit missing data; end-to-end exercises and updated guides demonstrate all guarantees without asserting unmeasured gains.

epic.title: Trustworthy completion and lighter agent orchestration

bundle.rationale:
Verification precedes throughput optimization. Four milestones separate (1) acceptance/artifact/increment invariants, (2) runtime check provenance, (3) scoped workers and deterministic supervision/recovery, and (4) adaptive execution and evaluation. Independent domain helpers can run in parallel; shared contracts and gate wiring have explicit dependencies. Every sprint has five coherent implementation tickets, one Fireguard ticket after those five, and its auto-created acceptance node. Human checkpoint approval remains mandatory. No run is started by this plan.

Compatibility: new decisions use explicit versioned verification policy; preserve completed plans/reports/hashes and never silently grandfather a new acceptance from missing legacy evidence. Provide explicit revalidation/migration for active work. Keep expected artifacts and check receipts distinct from subjective semantic review. A runtime receipt is process evidence under the local-host trust boundary, not cryptographic proof against an administrator with filesystem access.

Source identity: compare executable/configuration/test inputs, not an arbitrary branch name. Use a narrow versioned allowlist for generated DM bookkeeping; never blanket-exclude .darkmechanicus (profiles/project config may affect behavior). Capture source identity before and after checks, reject dirty/untracked relevant files, bind integration manifests and reused Fireguard to that identity, and invalidate on conflict resolution or source changes.

Preserve the owner's standing orchestrator model: the user's session coordinates; workers implement; the lighter mode reuses a worker context and still claims/reviews each ticket. It does not authorize the orchestrator to implement tickets or hand off the run. Hosted supervision gets deterministic process control; external hosts retain an explicit supported reporting route without fabricated liveness, capabilities or receipts.

Related backlog: ep_01m452vt115eqccd1ypdd596fy owns SPACE scores and comprehensive usage/timing ledgers (DM-169/170/172/173/175). This epic exports compatible raw evaluation observations and can run with those features absent, reporting unknown usage. Do not modify that epic or the in-flight Source control epic. No existing branch is selected or created during planning; bind an isolated feature branch from the agreed integrated base at execution.

Full DoD is read from the project at acceptance. Ticket workers run targeted checks only. Fireguard runs in each sprint's dedicated ticket with FIREGUARD_BASE_REF set to that sprint's start commit; full checks run once at acceptance, with rechecks only after changes invalidate evidence. Native/IPC work requires real Electron-path verification. Every phase must be exercised against its freshly built candidate in a scratch repository because the installed MCP server may predate the code being delivered.

Enforce the structural reviewer contract against the attempt's pinned ticket, inside the same transaction as the decision. Add a versioned compatibility policy: completed history is untouched; new decisions cannot use absent legacy evidence as proof. Newly saved strict tickets need criteria; old zero-criterion active tickets need explicit revalidation or a revised ticket, with an actionable error. Reviewer notes may supersede a worker's unmet finding only by an explicit verified result. Preserve decision idempotency and unauthorized-role checks.
